subtitle: Master expressive filter effects for dynamic tone control and musical phrasing

introduction.title: Understanding Filter Effects
introduction.text: Filter effects work by selectively emphasizing or reducing certain frequencies in your guitar signal. The wah pedal is the most famous filter effect, but the family includes auto-wahs, envelope filters, and various resonant filters. These effects can make your guitar "talk," add funk and expression, or create synthetic, otherworldly textures.
introduction.quote: The wah pedal doesn't just change your tone—it gives your guitar a voice, allowing you to shape each note's character in real-time and create the kind of expressive phrasing that defines funk, soul, and rock guitar.

cards.title: Basic Filtering Concepts
items: Bandpass Filter: Emphasizes a specific frequency range
Resonance/Q: How narrow and pronounced the filter peak is
Cutoff Frequency: The center frequency being emphasized
Sweep Range: The frequency range the filter can cover

cards.title: Control Methods
items: Manual: Foot pedal for real-time control
Auto-Wah: LFO sweeps the filter automatically
Envelope Filter: Your playing dynamics control the sweep
Expression Pedal: Hands-free continuous control

cards.title: Classic Wah Pedal
cards.description: Manual foot control of filter sweep, vocal-like "wah" sound, bandpass filter with resonance, inductor-based circuit (vintage models)

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Manual foot control of filter sweep, vocal-like "wah" sound, bandpass filter with resonance, inductor-based circuit (vintage models)

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Lead guitar expression, funk rhythm guitar, rock solos, creating talking guitar effects

fields.label: Famous Models
fields.value: Cry Baby, Vox V847, Wilson Shaft Wah

cards.title: Auto-Wah
cards.description: LFO-controlled filter sweep, rhythmic cyclic filtering, no foot control required

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: LFO-controlled filter sweep, rhythmic cyclic filtering, no foot control required, rate and depth controls

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Psychedelic textures, rhythmic emphasis, ambient soundscapes, consistent filtering patterns

cards.title: Envelope Filter
cards.description: Playing dynamics control filter, attack-sensitive response, quack/funk sound

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Playing dynamics control filter, attack-sensitive response, quack/funk sound, sensitivity and range controls

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Funk rhythm guitar, percussive playing styles, bass guitar (very popular), synth-like textures

fields.label: Famous Models
fields.value: Mutron III, MXR Envelope Filter, EHX Q-Tron

cards.title: Resonant Filters
cards.description: High resonance/Q settings, synthesizer-style filtering, can self-oscillate

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: High resonance/Q settings, synthesizer-style filtering, can self-oscillate, multiple filter types (LP, HP, BP)

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Electronic music, experimental sounds, industrial/noise music, sound design

fields.label: Toe vs. Heel
fields.value: Toe down = treble emphasis, heel down = bass emphasis. Most expressive range is in the middle.

fields.label: Rocking Motion
fields.value: Smooth, continuous rocking creates flowing wah sounds. Abrupt movements create percussive effects.

fields.label: Parking Positions
fields.value: Leave the pedal in specific positions for tonal colors: toe down for solos, heel down for rhythm.

fields.label: Note Timing
fields.value: Coordinate wah movement with note attacks for maximum expression. The wah should enhance, not fight, your phrasing.

fields.label: Bend Integration
fields.value: Combine wah sweeps with string bends for even more expressive range.

fields.label: Rhythm Patterns
fields.value: In funk, coordinate wah with chord stabs and muted notes for percussive effects.

cards.title: "Voodoo Child (Slight Return)" - Jimi Hendrix
cards.description: Cry Baby wah pedal with Marshall stack

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Aggressive rocking motion, coordinated with string bends, wide sweep range, high-gain amp interaction

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Defines the song's aggression, creates talking guitar effects, enhances Hendrix's expressiveness, became a wah template for rock

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Rhythmic chord stabs, synchronized with drums, parked in sweet spot, clean to slightly overdriven tone

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates funk groove foundation, adds percussive element, defines '70s soul/funk sound, emphasizes rhythmic pattern

cards.title: "White Room" - Cream
cards.description: Wah pedal parked in treble position

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Pedal in fixed toe-down position, no sweeping motion, bright cutting tone, used as tone shaper not effect

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates distinctive tonal character, cuts through dense mix, emphasizes high-end clarity, demonstrates static wah usage

cards.title: "Bulls on Parade" - Rage Against the Machine

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Pitch shifting controlled by expression, aggressive riff coordination, drop tuning with effect, percussive muting technique

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates aggressive, modern sound, defines Tom Morello's style, combines filtering with pitch effects, influences alternative/nu-metal

cards.title: Traditional Placement
items: Wah affects frequency content before distortion
Creates focused distortion character
Classic rock and blues sound
Natural, musical interaction

cards.title: Modern Placement
items: Wah shapes already-distorted signal
More dramatic filtering effects
Modern metal and alternative sound
Can create feedback issues at high gain

cards.title: What to Avoid
items: Constant, aimless sweeping without musical purpose
Fighting the song's rhythm with wah timing
Using wah on every single note or chord
Ignoring the sweet spots in the pedal's range
Poor foot technique causing inconsistent control

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Use wah to enhance musical phrases, not dominate them
Practice coordinating foot and hand movements
Learn to park the pedal in useful positions
Match wah intensity to the song's emotional content
Study how masters like Hendrix and Page use wah musically

fields.label: Heel-Toe Technique
fields.value: Quick heel-to-toe movements for percussive wah effects, especially effective in funk.

fields.label: Half-Cocked Wah
fields.value: Park the pedal partially engaged for a unique tonal color that cuts through a mix.

fields.label: Volume Swells
fields.value: Combine volume swells with wah sweeps for atmospheric, violin-like effects.

fields.label: MIDI Control
fields.value: Use MIDI controllers to precisely automate wah sweeps or control multiple parameters.

fields.label: Multi-Band Filtering
fields.value: Some modern pedals offer multiple frequency bands for more complex filtering.

fields.label: Envelope Following
fields.value: Let your playing dynamics control the wah automatically for hands-free expression.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Sweet Spot Discovery
items: Play sustained chords while slowly rocking the wah pedal through its entire range
Find the "quack" position (usually around 1/3 toe down)
Locate the smooth vocal position (around 2/3 toe down)
Identify the cutting lead position (full toe down)
Note the warm rhythm position (heel down)
These positions will become your go-to spots for different musical situations

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Rhythm Coordination
items: Practice a simple chord progression (Em - Am - Em - Am) with different wah patterns
On the beat: Move pedal with each chord change
Off the beat: Move pedal on the "and" of each beat
Syncopated: Create funky off-beat emphasis patterns
Static: Park in one position for each chord

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Lead Line Expression
items: Play a simple pentatonic phrase (A minor pentatonic works well)
One sweep per phrase
One sweep per note
Emphasizing specific notes with quick sweeps
Combining with string bends for maximum expression
